name: metabolism-biomass-yield
title: Is v2ecoli's central carbon metabolism physically correct?

glossary.definition: Grams of dry cell weight produced per gram of glucose consumed, here computed by direct mass balance as dDW / integral(q_glc * DW) dt over post-burn-in cells.
The maximum Yxs a carbon- and energy-balanced cell can achieve, 0.538 gDW/g glucose from Varma 1993 (FBA, fully aerobic, no maintenance energy). A model above it is forbidden, not merely unusual.

The ratio of carbon accounted for on the output side (CO2, secreted acetate, biomass) to carbon entering as glucose. A value near 1 means the books balance; the binding-cap overflow condition reaches 7.93, meaning carbon is created.
CO2 evolved per O2 consumed. Full glucose oxidation gives ~1; the v2ecoli baseline gives ~3.6, indicating it barely respires.

question: Does the v2ecoli baseline conserve carbon and respect the thermodynamic ceiling on biomass yield? The basal population_phenotype_basal vs_literature card grades physiology.biomass_yield at 0.826 gDW/g glucose against a measured band of 0.355-0.444 and a first-principles ceiling of 0.538, a verdict of first_principles_violation that has stood committed since 2026-06-17. This investigation is named for that failing axis and carries no hypothesis about mechanism.

executive.what_is_this: A model-correctness thread on v2ecoli's central carbon metabolism, opened because the baseline produces more biomass per gram of glucose than carbon and energy balance permit. The object of evaluation is the model - a defect with a fix at the end - as distinct from the sibling metabolism-overflow investigation, which evaluates a method.
executive.verdict: CONFIRMED and LOCALISED. A fresh 4x8 run on a recorded commit gives Yxs 0.831 gDW/g glucose - 1.87x the top of the measured band and 1.55x the first-principles ceiling - reproducing the committed fixture's 0.826 to within 0.67%, so the violation is real and not an artefact of the fixtures' unrecorded provenance. The same run localises it: carbon accounting stays self-consistent at baseline (implied biomass carbon 0.455 gC/gDW, inside the physically plausible range), while respiration is nearly absent (O2:glucose 0.096, RQ 3.43 against ~1) and 94.5% of glucose carbon is retained as biomass. The baseline defect is therefore ENERGETIC - biomass built without paying its ATP cost - and distinct from the mass-bookkeeping failure that appears under a binding uptake cap. The fix should be scoped around maintenance-ATP and respiratory capacity, not around mass accounting.

decisions_needed.question: Is the baseline yield violation one defect with the binding-cap carbon creation, or two?
decisions_needed.status: RESOLVED (2026-07-29, S1) - two distinct defects. Carbon conserves at baseline while yield violates the ceiling; a single bookkeeping bug would break conservation everywhere and does not.
decisions_needed.context: The overflow study's finding concludes the violation points at the same bookkeeping problem as carbon-created-under-binding-uptake-cap. That is the hypothesis S1 tests, not its premise. The signatures differ: at a slack cap carbon closure is 1.11 (books nearly close) while yield is ~2x the ceiling; under a binding cap closure degrades to 7.93 and carbon is created. A pure bookkeeping bug should break conservation everywhere, so the baseline behaviour points instead at an energetic defect.
decisions_needed.resolution: S1 measured implied biomass carbon at 0.4549 gC/gDW on 20 cells at commit 84383530 - squarely inside the 0.45-0.50 gC/gDW a real E. coli has - so the model is not creating carbon at baseline. It is failing to burn any: O2:glucose 0.096, CO2:glucose 0.331, RQ 3.43, 94.5% of glucose carbon to biomass. Two defects, and only the baseline one is in scope for this investigation. CAVEAT: S1 computes biomass carbon by difference, which fixes the closure ratio at 1.0 by construction and moves the information into the implied carbon content; that content is the evidence. It is therefore not a like-for-like comparison against the overflow's 1.11 / 7.93, which use an independent biomass-carbon estimate. Strong positive evidence, not proof. Making it like-for-like needs the overflow runner's closure estimator, which lives only on that branch.

decisions_needed.question: How should implied biomass carbon content be graded absolutely, rather than only by contrast against another condition?
decisions_needed.context: S1 deliberately makes no absolute claim about the 0.455 gC/gDW it measured, because the only in-repo reference for that quantity does not survive inspection. The range ~0.45-0.50 gC/gDW at scripts/render_basal_vs_literature.py:77 is an uncited constant introduced 2026-06-17; its units may be a slip from biomass YIELD (gDW/g glucose), whose curated band overlaps the same numeric window so the error leaves no trace; tests/test_basal_vs_literature.py:122 independently uses 0.40-0.55 for the same quantity; and there is no biomass-carbon-content key anywhere in the ecoli-sources validation bundle, unlike the ten other basal__* observables.
options: PREFERRED - grade against the model's OWN composition-derived carbon content. The model knows its biomass composition, so its carbon content follows; disagreement between that and the flux-derived number IS non-conservation, decided internally with no literature required. Blocked on sim_data (bake_model_metabolism._load() needs out/sim_data_full/parca_state.pkl.gz, absent in the s3 worktree).

Tiered band on the yield-axis pattern (expected / questionable / first-principles violation). Note the failure directions invert relative to intuition: because the quantity is computed BY DIFFERENCE, carbon CREATION drives implied content DOWN (the leftover cannot pay for the biomass built) and carbon LOSS drives it UP. So a hard ceiling guards the less interesting direction. A >1.0 gC/gDW ceiling is free - biomass cannot exceed 100% carbon, which is arithmetic, not biology - while a tighter ~0.8 bound (no whole cell approaches even pure lipid at ~0.77 gC/g) costs an argument.
Curate a basal__biomass_carbon_content key into ecoli-sources with a real citation, matching how the other ten observables are handled.

scientific_argument.main_claim: The v2ecoli baseline violates the first-principles ceiling on biomass yield while still conserving carbon, which localises the baseline defect to the energetic side of metabolism rather than to mass bookkeeping.
evidence_for: S1, fresh 4x8 run at commit 84383530, 20 post-burn-in cells, direct mass balance: Yxs = 0.8313 gDW/g glucose (CV 1.44%) against a measured band of 0.355-0.444 and a theoretical_max of 0.538 - 1.87x the top of the band and 1.55x the ceiling.
The committed fixture reproduces: 0.8313 fresh vs 0.8257 baked, a 0.67% difference inside the ensemble CV, so the 2026-06-17 verdict is not an artefact of the fixtures' unrecorded provenance.
Carbon conserves at baseline: implied biomass carbon 0.4549 gC/gDW sits inside the 0.45-0.50 range a real E. coli has, so this is not mass creation.
The baseline barely respires: O2:glucose 0.096, CO2:glucose 0.331, RQ 3.43 against ~1 for full oxidation, leaving 94.5% of glucose carbon in biomass and almost none burned for maintenance and ATP.
caveats: The 0.826 figure comes from committed fixtures stamped reconstructed: True, commit: None, sweep_dir: None, baked: unknown. The code and sweep that produced it were never recorded, so it cannot be attributed to any particular revision. Removing that ambiguity is S1's first duty.

The equivalence reference mode cannot see this defect. v2ecoli is a port of v1 with byte-level equivalence demonstrated, so if both share the defect the card returns within_tol on a thermodynamically forbidden number. Correctness evidence has to come from the literature / first-principles side.

studies.name: population_phenotype_basal
studies.title: Basal-condition physiology — v2ecoli baseline vs experimental literature
studies.question:
Does the v2ecoli baseline single-cell→division ensemble reproduce the
basal-condition physiology of glucose-minimal MG1655 — growth rate, biomass
yield, glucose uptake, central-carbon fluxes, exchange rates, proteome census,
macromolecular composition, and metabolite pools — when graded against curated
experimental + theoretical reference values rather than a pinned run?

findings.statement: The baseline ensemble makes 0.826 gDW of biomass per gram of glucose consumed — 1.86× the top of the measured band (0.355–0.444) and 1.54× the first-principles ceiling of 0.538. No carbon- and energy-balanced cell can exceed that ceiling, so this is a model defect, not a calibration mismatch. The dispersion is tight (CV 1.55% across 20 cells), so it is a systematic property of the model rather than noise. Carbon is nonetheless conserved at baseline — implied biomass carbon ≈ 0.457 gC/gDW is physically plausible — which locates the defect on the energetic side: the ensemble barely respires (O₂:glucose ≈ 0.09, CO₂:glucose ≈ 0.33, RQ ≈ 3.6 against ~1 for full oxidation), so almost no glucose carbon is burned for maintenance and ATP, and nearly all of it is retained as biomass.

evidence.provenance_limitation: The measured side is the committed tests/fixtures/population_phenotype_basal/ fixtures, which stamp reconstructed: True, commit: None, sweep_dir: None, baked: unknown. The exact code and sweep that produced 0.826 were never recorded, so this value cannot be attributed to any particular revision of the model.

expected.summary: Measured band 0.355–0.444 gDW/g glucose from four aerobic glucose-minimal determinations — varma_1994 (0.355, W3110 aerobic batch), kavvas_2022 (0.42, ¹³C-MFA MG1655), lacroix_2015 (0.44, MG1655 M9), long_2017 (0.444, ¹³C-MFA MG1655). The threshold is the first-principles ceiling, varma_1993 = 0.538 (FBA, fully aerobic, no maintenance energy); a value above it is forbidden by carbon and energy balance rather than merely unusual.

findings.next_action: Re-measure Yxs on a fresh basal run whose commit is recorded, and compute carbon closure and RQ on the same run, to establish whether the baseline defect is energetic and distinct from the carbon creation seen under a binding uptake cap. Tracked as study metabolism-biomass-yield-s1-diagnostic.

studies.name: metabolism-biomass-yield-s1-diagnostic
studies.title: Re-measure biomass yield on a recorded commit, and discriminate one defect from two
studies.question: On a fresh basal run whose code revision is recorded, what is the biomass yield - and does carbon close at the same time? The first half removes the provenance ambiguity in the committed fixtures; the second half is the discriminator, because if carbon closes at baseline while yield sits above the first-principles ceiling, the baseline defect is energetic and therefore distinct from the carbon creation seen under a binding uptake cap.

findings.statement: On a run whose commit is recorded, the baseline makes 0.831 gDW per gram of glucose - 1.87x the top of the measured band and 1.55x the first-principles ceiling - and the run shows no sign of the gross carbon imbalance that appears under a binding uptake cap. Implied biomass carbon comes out at 0.455 gC/gDW, an ordinary value, against a binding-cap condition where closure degrades to 7.93. The comparison that carries this is RELATIVE: two conditions of the same model behaving qualitatively differently. A single mass-bookkeeping defect would break conservation in both. What the baseline fails to do is respire: O2:glucose is 0.096 and RQ is 3.43 against ~1 for full oxidation, so 94.5% of glucose carbon is retained as biomass and almost none is burned for maintenance and ATP. The violation is therefore energetic in origin - the cell builds biomass it never pays the ATP cost for - and is a different failure from the carbon creation the binding cap triggers. Two defects, not one.

expected.summary: A pure mass-bookkeeping defect should break carbon conservation everywhere it is exercised. The overflow titration shows closure of 1.11 at a slack cap and 7.93 under a binding cap, so if one bug drove both, baseline carbon accounting should also be visibly broken. It is not.

findings.next_action: Scope the fix around the energetic side - maintenance-ATP / NGAM-GAM parameterization and respiratory capacity - rather than around mass bookkeeping. Enzyme-capacity constraints remain downstream of this: they bite when a cell pushes respiration to its ceiling, and this model barely respires.

findings.statement: The fresh run gives Yxs 0.8313 against the committed fixture's 0.8257, a difference of 0.67% - well inside the ensemble CV of 1.44%. Growth rate 0.851 vs 0.814 and glucose uptake 4.81 vs 5.14 are likewise close. So the fixture's headline number is reproducible on current main even though its provenance was never recorded, and the first_principles_violation verdict standing since 2026-06-17 is not an artefact of a stale or unattributable bake.

expected.summary: The committed fixtures stamp reconstructed: True, commit: None, sweep_dir: None, baked: unknown, so agreement was not guaranteed and a material divergence would itself have been the finding.

findings.next_action: No re-bake. The fixtures are the reference everything else is graded against and moving them mid-investigation shifts that reference; this run is evidence for #296 (auto re-bake / re-grade), not a reason to pre-empt it.

studies.name: metabolism-biomass-yield-s1b-anaerobic-contrast
studies.title: Does the model's own aerobic-to-anaerobic yield drop match biology?
studies.question: Real E. coli anaerobic biomass yield is several-fold below aerobic, because without a terminal electron acceptor the cell cannot extract ATP by respiration. A model that barely respires aerobically (O2:glucose ~0.09, RQ ~3.6) has little respiratory contribution to lose, so it should show a much smaller drop. Does it? This is a first-principles discriminator that needs no external reference data - the model is compared against its own aerobic result.
